newsitem.title: UK: UK women criticise "demeaning" advertising - survey.
newsitem.headline: UK women criticise "demeaning" advertising - survey.

text.p: Women are more influenced by advertising that portrays them as independent-minded and strong, but many ads remain demeaning, according to a survey of British women released on Monday.

Of the women surveyed, 56 percent said they were more likely to be influenced by advertising that portrayed them in a "positive light" and 49 percent said they found much advertising demeaning, Britain's Channel 4 television network reported.
The survey was conducted for Channel 4's annual "Talking to Women" conference. Channel 4 is one of the UK's three commercial television networks.

"Women still feel advertisements portray them in a negative light, and this appears to be working against client interests," Ruth Roscorla, business development manager at Channel 4, said in a statement.
Car and financial services advertising were singled out by women surveyed as being flawed in their advertising approach.
